name: Mobile app
summary: Installed apps held in one hand: iOS and Android, native or cross-platform, used in short interrupted sessions.
summaryVi: Ứng dụng đã cài, cầm bằng một tay: iOS và Android, native hay cross-platform, dùng trong những phiên ngắn và hay bị ngắt quãng.
optimisesFor: One thumb, on a screen that will be interrupted before the task is finished.

skill.name: mobile-app-design
skill.description: Design, build, restyle or review mobile app interfaces for iOS and Android - tab bars, navigation bars, list screens, detail screens, bottom sheets, forms over a keyboard, onboarding and permission prompts. Use it whenever creating or changing how a phone or tablet app screen looks or behaves: reach, touch targets, gestures, safe areas, sheets, keyboard avoidance, spacing, typography, states or motion; when asked to make an app screen look better, cleaner or more native; when asked where a button or a navigation item should go on a phone; when a screen must survive being backgrounded, rotated or interrupted mid-task; or when porting a desktop or web screen to a phone. Covers SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, React Native, Flutter and mobile web alike. Not for desktop admin panels, marketing sites or any interface used with a mouse at desk distance.
skill.descriptionVi: Thiết kế, dựng, chỉnh lại hoặc review giao diện ứng dụng di động iOS và Android.

when: an installed app on a phone or tablet, native or cross-platform
a screen operated with a thumb rather than a cursor
a question about where a control belongs on a small screen
a screen that must survive being backgrounded, rotated or interrupted
porting a desktop or web screen down to a phone
notFor: desktop admin panels, operations consoles and anything used with a mouse at desk distance - use the erp pack
marketing sites and landing pages, even the ones read on a phone - use the consumer-web pack, which optimises for a stranger's first five seconds rather than for a returning user's thumb
dense data tables and any screen whose job is to show twenty rows at once
watch, TV and spatial interfaces, whose input and viewing distance are different problems again

surfaces.chrome: the tab bar and the navigation bar - translucent over the content, flush with the system, never a frame around it
surfaces.canvas: the scrolling content itself; there is no separate page background behind it
surfaces.content: list rows separated by inset dividers, not cards
surfaces.floating: sheets that rise from the bottom edge - the dominant modal form; dialogs are the exception
surfaces.accent: one value per surface, and it marks the single primary action per screen
surfaces.semantic: success/warning/danger/info, with danger reserved for what cannot be undone

platform.note: One thumb, on a device held while walking. 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android are the platform floors; this pack treats them as the floor and puts anything used often into the reachable arc at the bottom.

density: comfortable - 17pt/16sp body, 44pt minimum row height, 16pt screen margins

overrides.rule: core/03-layout.md: never remove functionality at a smaller size - change its form
overrides.why: A phone is not a smaller size of something, it is the only size. This pack removes functionality outright rather than compacting it: a secondary report, a bulk edit, a twelve-column table are moved to the web app and linked, because the compacted version of each one is worse than an honest absence. The core rule protects a responsive layout from dropping features as the viewport narrows; it is not a mandate to fit a desktop feature set onto a phone.
